name: Tuomo Suntola
summary: Finnish electrical engineer and inventor who pioneered the ALD/ALE thin-film growth technique.

name: Helsinki University of Technology
summary: Major Finnish technical university where Suntola studied and earned his doctorate.

name: VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland
summary: Finnish national research organization where Suntola worked on early sensor development.

name: Instrumentarium Oy
summary: Finnish medical equipment manufacturer where Suntola established a research group in 1974.

name: Lohja Oy
summary: Finnish industrial company that acquired Suntola's ALE-EL project in 1978.

name: Microchemistry Ltd.
summary: Company founded by Suntola in 1987 to commercialize ALE for solar, catalysis, and semiconductor applications.

name: ASM
summary: Dutch company that acquired Microchemistry in 1999, continuing ALE reactor manufacturing.

name: Planar Inc.
summary: American flat panel display manufacturer that acquired Lohja's EL business in 1990.

name: Tampere
summary: Finnish city where Suntola was born.

name: Espoo
summary: Finnish city where Suntola moved his research group in 1974 and where Lohja built its EL production facility.

name: Atomic Layer Epitaxy
summary: Sequential gas-solid deposition method invented by Suntola in 1974, later renamed ALD.

name: Humicap 1
summary: Capacitive humidity sensor developed by Suntola at VTT in 1973.

name: European SEMI Award
summary: Industry recognition presented by SEMI in 2004 honoring Suntola as a pioneer in ALD techniques.

name: Jorma Antson
summary: Finnish researcher who collaborated with Suntola on humidity sensors and ALE-EL displays.

name: Sven Lindfors
summary: Finnish reactor designer who worked closely with Suntola on ALE equipment development.

name: Arto Pakkala
summary: Finnish engineer who contributed to ALE-EL development and reactor design.

name: Tapio Wiik
summary: Finnish researcher who conducted pre-studies for Suntola's humidity sensor project.

name: Lauri Niinistö
summary: Finnish chemistry professor who collaborated with Suntola on ALE surface chemistry.

name: Antti Piippo
summary: Business manager who led Lohja's Display Electronics division and later founded Elcoteq.
